statements.text: Normal trades can be made to fail for any pair of amounts with disjoint bits, enabling denial of service on order execution.
evidence: Because base amounts are denominated in base tokens and quote amounts in quote tokens, equality is virtually impossible, so every trade relies on the bit-wise clause. Random bit patterns therefore decide whether normal trades succeed or fail, enabling denial-of-service on any pair of amounts with disjoint bits.
High – attacker can systematically revert genuine matches, effectively freezing order execution and denying service.

statements.text: Inferred: the zero-amount guard should reject a trade only when either side is actually zero, allowing legitimate non-zero trades to complete.
evidence: [`_processLimitBidOrder()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-07-gte-clob/blob/2783108d14010ae50f2a5f65c3a9c94e2e7845b9/contracts/clob/CLOB.sol#L492-L531) and [`_processLimitAskOrder()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-07-gte-clob/blob/2783108d14010ae50f2a5f65c3a9c94e2e7845b9/contracts/clob/CLOB.sol#L533-L571) use a bit-wise AND (`&`) instead of a logical check to detect zero-amount trades, causing legitimate trades to revert with `ZeroCostTrade`.
The developer’s intention is to throw when either side of the trade is zero.
